subject: Anthropology
title: Disability and Culture
description: A short lesson to help you apply Disability and Culture.

hook.text: A deaf person in Martha's Vineyard wasn't disabled — everyone there signed. Disability depends on context.

buildup.text: The social model of disability argues that people are disabled by barriers in society, not by their bodies alone.

discovery.text: Cultures define disability differently. What's disabling in one society may be normal or even valued in another.

twist.text: The medical model treats disability as individual defect. The social model reveals it as a product of excluding design.

climax.text: Disability is cultural, not just medical. Changing the environment changes who is disabled and who isn't.

punchline.text: Society disables people more than bodies do.

quiz.question: What does the social model of disability argue?
options: Disability is purely a medical condition
People are disabled by social barriers, not just their bodies

details.summary: Disability is culturally defined — what counts as disability, how disabled people are treated, and what accommodations exist vary enormously. The medical model treats disability as individual pathology while the social model locates disability in environmental and attitudinal barriers.
details.whyItMatters: The shift from medical to social models of disability transforms how societies respond to impairment. Understanding disability as socially constructed leads to environmental accommodation rather than individual cure.
takeaways: Disability is culturally defined, not purely biological
The medical model treats disability as individual pathology
The social model locates disability in environmental barriers

faq.question: What is the social model of disability?
faq.answer: The social model argues that impairment becomes disability through social barriers — stairs instead of ramps, visual-only information, employment discrimination. A wheelchair user is disabled by stairs, not by their body. Removing barriers removes disability without changing the individual.

faq.question: How do different cultures treat disability?
faq.answer: Some cultures view disability as spiritual gift or ancestral communication. Others stigmatize it as punishment or contamination. Western societies increasingly adopt rights-based approaches. The variation demonstrates that disability is a social category, not just a medical condition.
